claim: A typed field is not one shape. Four distinct mechanisms were hidden behind the same ENTER verb: a transformation named after the quote, an answer printed on the page, one token across several fields, and a native control that owns its own editor.

measurement.instrument: full 130 tasks x 5 reps, page identity per rep, exclusive CDP browser
measurement.note: t=1.88 < 1.98. NOT significant on its own, and it does not need to be: the four repaired tasks were 0/5 each and are now 5/5 each, verified individually at 8-10 reps.

enter-text-2.mechanism: the goal names a transformation of the quoted token ('in all lower case letters'); typed verbatim it is a certain failure

text-transform.mechanism: constant goal, answer printed in #captcha as one skewed <span> per character

enter-password.mechanism: scores #password AND #verify; the old path filled one box

enter-date.mechanism: native input[type=date] ignores keystrokes; page wants YYYY-MM-DD, goal quotes mm/dd/yyyy

regression_check.method: every DOWN task re-measured at 10 reps
regression_check.verdict: NO regression attributable to this round: every rerun lands between the two readings. But these tasks are genuinely UNSTABLE (use-autocomplete 0.60/0.20/0.10 across three readings of the same code), and that instability is what the learning loop is supposed to fix and never has.

instrument_bugs_found: click_el resolves an expression to an ELEMENT. Returning !!es[i] hands it `true` and the press silently never happens.
input[type=text] does not match input[type=date] -- the date task was typing at a box that was not there.
The decomposer turns 'Enter 12/03/2017 as the date' into token='12'. Any rule keyed on the token sees a truncated number; the date has to be parsed from the goal.
The decomposer turns 'Type the text below' into token='the' (length 3), so a len<3 guard does not fire. Guard on _ARTICLES too.
next: The typed field is now covered. The remaining mass is not a control shape at all: 10 email tasks and 3 social-media tasks are one app each, and they need an app-level procedure rather than a widget verb.
